task_title: Fix epic-reprocess staleness + merge-train quarantine repair

plan_review.notes: gpt-5.4 (high effort) reviewed the design (not just code) after reading epic-reprocess.mjs, issue-intake-lib.mjs, quarantine-repair.mjs/test, reconcile.mjs quarantine path, reconcile-lib.mjs. Verdict was rejected pending fixes; all 9 concerns resolved, no re-architecture. Alternatives considered and rejected: (1) always restart:true for Copilot-assigned epic nodes -- rejected, would restart healthy sessions, violates rule; (2) make Fix-1 purely event-driven off PR close/quarantine instead of a polling backstop -- rejected, reconcile.mjs already restarts on PR-close, this IS the backstop for when that misses, duplication is intentional defense-in-depth, documented in code comment; (3) repair inline at the quarantine site in reconcile.mjs instead of a separate post-pass sweep -- rejected, keeps the quarantine-detection concern (reconcile.mjs) separate from the repair concern (quarantine-repair.mjs), and the sweep re-derives the confirmation from the same authoritative marker so no information is lost; (4) change GitHub App/branch permissions to let the train push copilot/* directly -- rejected, outside repo control (GitHub-enforced Copilot-branch restriction), and would remove the branch-owner safety property intentionally. Must-fix #5 (BLOCKED_LABEL is generic -- also applied by blockEntry/deAdmitNoop for validation failures and no-op diffs, both commonly on copilot/* branches too) -- fixed by adding isConfirmedRestrictedBranchQuarantine(), which reads the authoritative evaluateUnadvanceableStrike status-comment marker (same one the quarantine path itself writes) and requires strikes >= UNADVANCEABLE_STRIKE_THRESHOLD for the CURRENT live head sha; repairQuarantinedPr now calls this before ever creating a branch/PR. Must-fix #6 (existing-PR reuse on a branch was accepted without validating base/marker) -- fixed by findVerifiedReplacementPr(), which requires the found open PR to carry the exact repair marker for (originalPrNumber, headSha) and target the expected base, else throws rather than silently linking. Nice-to-have #7 (ref-creation race) -- hardened: POST /git/refs now catches a 422 and re-verifies the sha before accepting. Nice-to-have #8 (labels(first:50) could truncate merge-train-blocked off a heavily-labeled PR) -- bumped to first:100. Nice-to-have #9 (notice-marker suppression trusted any commenter) -- fixed by isTrustedNoticeAuthor(), reusing the performed_via_github_app / TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS / TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS pattern already established in issue-intake-lib.mjs/reconcile.mjs, so only our own automation identity (or another trusted actor) can suppress a re-post. All fixes covered by new/updated node --test cases (19 tests in quarantine-repair.test.mjs, 13 in epic-reprocess.test.mjs); full targeted suite re-run clean (1135 tests) after each fix.

rounds.notes: copilotOwnershipStatus treated a MERGED linked PR the same as CLOSED (both fell outside the state===open filter), so an issue could be spuriously restarted during the merge-vs-issue-autoclose webhook lag window. Fixed: MERGED now short-circuits to stale:false before the abandoned/quarantined checks; 2 new regression tests added.

Re-reviewed full diff after the MERGED fix. Confirmed PullRequestState GraphQL enum has only OPEN/CLOSED/MERGED (no other value hits this bug class); REST PR state (used in quarantine-repair.mjs repairEligibility) has only open/closed, no analogous issue. No further findings across epic-reprocess.mjs, issue-intake-lib.mjs, quarantine-repair.mjs(+test), merge-train.yml, merge-train-workflow-wakeups.test.ts.

independent_grade.notes: Inspected the complete diff between the merge base and HEAD across all touched files. The implementation for epic-reprocess staleness accurately identifies abandoned or quarantined PRs, and correctly forces an unassign/reassign sequence to trigger the issue-intake webhook. The quarantine-repair logic is defensively written, checking original markers, handling concurrent races gracefully, and strictly verifying ancestry before touching branches. Test coverage is thorough, directly verifying the new logic and the workflow integrations. Overall, a robust and policy-compliant resolution.
